Subject: QBR slate governance and failure-modes - draft review

Team / Marta —

Attached is the working draft of the QBR slate (qbr_slate_draft_v3.pdf) and a focused dependency map (dependency_map.xlsx). This thread is to:

- Surface the gating criteria we plan to present to the execs for the hoster launch.
- Capture known failure-modes and proposed mitigations we want on the slide deck.
- Lock owners on any items that must be resolved before the QBR (next Thu).

High level asks (please action before end of day Friday):
1) Aditya — confirm which of the infra risks in the dependency_map are mitigation-ready vs require vendor escalations. Mark with owner + ETA.
2) Irene — update the compliance slide with any outstanding evidence requested by Greenfield Health (Marta) and confirm SOC2 checklist status.
3) Monica / Vivek — decide whether we present the soft SLA exception as an open risk or request an SLA waiver from Finance.

Marta — appreciate any customer-facing concerns to call out; we plan to show the impact matrix rather than raw incident counts.

Attachments: qbr_slate_draft_v3.pdf, dependency_map.xlsx, failure_modes_summary.docx

Thanks —
Laura

On Thu, Sep 3, 2026 at 8:12 AM Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team / Marta —
> 
> Attached is the working draft of the QBR slate ...

Quick engineering notes / reality check: 

- Dependency_map.xlsx: rows highlighted in orange are blocking (vendor bug, kernel mismatch, infra quota). I added short notes in column H with the minimal mitigation path.
- Mitigation-ready: autoscaling fallback, KV cache TTL rollback, and the temporary model pin (v2.1-static) are all deployable by next Tue EOD with the current on-call rota.
- Vendor escalations needed: Zion Cloud kernel regression (ticket #Z-4092) — we need a vendor SLA commitment to finish the backport. Without it, our latency SLO for sequences >2k may slip by ~30-45%.
- Failure_modes_summary.docx includes three new failure-cases: (1) cache staleness under high fanout, (2) cross-tenant memory bleed on older CUDA drivers, (3) degraded accuracy after quantization fallback. I added probable impact and short-term rollback steps.

Ask: can we run a short canary (50 queries/min for 2h) against v2.1-static in staging tomorrow morning? If yes I'll schedule and capture traces for the deck.

-Aditya
Aditya Rao
Staff Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
aditya_rao@redwood.com

Thanks, all — good framing. A few decisions from leadership side: 

- We will present the soft-SLA as a controlled risk. Monica, please prepare a one-slide rationale that explains: why we are asking for an exception, the exact customer impact window, and the remediation timeline.
- Aditya: proceed with the canary. If traces show regression above 20% for tail latency we escalate to Zion and pause the broader rollout.
- Irene: if Greenfield needs additional compliance evidence to accept our private deployment, we should surface that as a conditional acceptance in the customer slide. Marta, please flag the minimum acceptable evidence.

Meeting: I'll chair a 30m sync tomorrow 9:00–9:30am PT to triage blockers and lock owners. Monica to own the minute notes and action tracker.

One more thing — we need a short 'failure-mode decision tree' graphic for the deck (two-box flow: severity -> immediate action). Aditya / Design — can you produce a simple SVG by EOD Friday?

-Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
VP Product & Ops
